newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian kidnappers release Italian engineer.
newsitem.headline: Colombian kidnappers release Italian engineer.

text.p: An Italian engineer kidnapped by leftist guerrillas while working on an oil pipeline project in northern Colombia was released on Wednesday after a five-month ordeal, a senior Colombian army official said.

The official, who asked not to be identified by name but who works with an anti-kidnapping force called Gaula, said Lino Chioccioli, 49, was freed in northwestern Antioquia province. He said he could not provide details of the release.
Chioccioli was kidnapped by National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels in August after he landed by helicopter at a construction site near the Caribbean coast, the official said.
The ELN, founded by radical Roman Catholic priests in 1966 and Colombia's second largest guerrilla group, specialises in kidnappings and attacks on oil and coal projects.

Chioccioli's employer, Italian oil and gas exploration company Saipem, said in Rome an anonymous phone caller to the Italian Embassy in Bogota gave the first news of his release. The company did not provide any details on his condition and embassy officials could not be immediately be reached for comment.
Saipem thanked Italy's foreign ministry and religious and humanitarian groups that helped in efforts to secure Chioccioli's release.

His daughter, Deborah, interviewed by the Italian news agency ANSA at her home in Arezzo, central Italy, said she did not want to discuss negotiations which resulted in his release. "We are happy but we don't want to say anything else. It's logical that there were negotiations ... Maybe we will recount them in a few days," she was quoted as saying.
